messages:
incident-bot: PAGED - Observability alert: high ingestion latency for Datadog traces & custom metrics in eu-west-1. Dashboards not updating; alert backlog increasing.
Nadia R (infra-oncall): Confirming. Grafana panels for EU clusters stalled ~20m. Traces for routes behind nginx-eu are absent.
Jon P (SRE): Datadog API status calls are returning intermittent 502s. Pulling raw logs from ELK shows normal traffic. No user-facing errors from healthcheck endpoints.
Lina K (customer-success): A handful of enterprise customers pinged support about missing traces and historic charts. They're worried about SLA/reporting windows.
Nadia R: Opening Datadog ticket now: https://support.datadoghq.com/ticket/RW-55621 - flagged as high.
Datadog Support: "Thanks for reporting. We're seeing ingestion delays in eu-west-1 affecting traces and some custom metrics. Investigating backlog. We'll update."
Jon P: Mitigation plan: (1) enable emergency pushgateway/remote_write to fallback metrics collector (2) route critical alerts to CloudWatch where possible (3) export app spans/logs to S3 for forensic analysis (4) raise alert suppression for noisy alerts so oncall isn't overwhelmed.
Nadia R: Executing rollouts:
```bash
kubectl -n monitoring apply -f emergency-remote-write.yaml
kubectl -n monitoring scale deployment prometheus-emergency --replicas=2
```
ops-bot: Automation note: alert reroute job started (job-id: reroute-eu-556).
Jon P: Patch applied for two critical SLOs: payments-api and ingest-worker now use cloudwatch fallback. Adding annotations to runbooks.
Lina K: I'll send a short proactive note to impacted Dedicated/Private EU tenants explaining observability delays and that our engineering team is on it.
Nadia R: Starting raw span export for namespaces payments and ingest into s3://redwood-emergency/eu-obsv/2734509876/ (48h retention).
Jon P: Running throttles for non-critical alerts: `./scripts/throttle_alerts --region eu-west --priority low` to reduce noise.
Datadog Support: "Backlog identified. Processing will take time; some metrics and traces may appear delayed or out of order during the backfill."
Nadia R: Heads up: backfilled points might create spikes. Do not auto-resolve alerts until we've validated post-backfill baselines.
Platform Eng: started a temporary sidecar re-forwarder on nginx-eu to attempt span flushes to Datadog collector endpoints.
Jon P: Handoff: I'll take primary for mitigation; Nadia handing off in 20m. Nadia please include config changes in the incident doc.
Nadia R: Handoff done ". handing off to @Jon P". Documented steps and exported logs. Synthetic checks remain green.
ops-bot: Incident severity currently P2 (observability loss only).
Datadog Support: update: "Backfill in progress; estimated catch-up 30-60 minutes. We'll notify when streams return to normal."
Jon P: Seeing traces trickle back for ingest-worker. Metrics are starting to populate but some series out-of-order. Monitoring for alert flaps.
Lina K: Customer comms sent to the small set that reported issues. One customer (omega-inc) asked for ETA - I've looped their AM.
Datadog Support: update: "Ingestion catch-up complete for eu-west-1. Pipelines nominal."
Jon P: Verified dashboards rehydrate and traces appear. Cleanup actions: revert alert reroutes, disable emergency exporters after 24h, run reconciliation job between CloudWatch and Datadog metrics to identify any alerts caused by backfill.
Lina K: Preparing external summary and will coordinate with marketing/legal if customers request formal incident writeup.
ops-bot: Incident resolved in channel. Reopen if regression observed.
Jon P: Follow-ups: create postmortem, update Datadog incident runbook with our mitigation playbook, and evaluate dual-path alerting for EU. Assigning owners now.
Platform Eng: Adding resilience tasks to backlog (longer-term: multi-sink telemetry for critical EU services).
Lina K: Thanks team. We'll close customer loop after postmortem and provide customers a short explanation of mitigations taken.
